question: what is the committed state that the calibrated magnitude, added as an opt-in parameter with default 1.0, must leave untouched?
claim: With the calibrated magnitude at its default of 1.0, NOTHING changes: every committed .bio programme under data/organisms, genomeos/std and data/demo is byte-identical to the bytes digested here, and every count in this census -- the `bio test` file count and checks-passed total, each programme's entity and rule count, and each programme's declared `# test:` lines, chr21's `# test: rules == 5176` among them -- is unchanged. The parameter is opt-in: a run gets the measured magnitude only by asking for it by name, and no default run and no committed programme asks
verification: sha256 over the bytes of each programme, plus one group digest over all of them in a fixed order, plus the counts recomputed by running `bio test`'s own checks in process. `--verify` recomputes every field of this record and compares field by field, printing the first mismatch with both values. Byte digests and integer counts, never a reading of a diff and never an eyeballed count: the error this guards against is a change that looks inert in a diff and moves a number

magnitude.reading: M2h: on genes held out of the fit, the multiplicative composition scaled by the one factor fitted on the training genes came closer to measured RNA than the no-rule baseline (held-out Delta MSE +0.04339 [98.33% CI +0.0379, +0.04894] over 108,264 gene-cell pairs, 8,328 genes; control p = 0.000999; fitted scale +0.2146 [98.33% CI +0.2007, +0.2283]), about 2% of the measured variance
magnitude.it_is_a_global_average: lane-scalehet/hetblock2 (`d9e3ddd`) measured that the magnitude is NOT one global number: it varies by chromosome and that heterogeneity survives a locus-block null. +0.2146 is a global AVERAGE over a varying magnitude and must be described that way
magnitude.nothing_is_fitted_here: the constant is read from ac5580b; this lane fits nothing

does_not_claim: this census says nothing about RNA, about whether the calibrated composition predicts expression, or about whether the default SHOULD be 1.0. It is a record of the committed state and of one safety property of an addition to it. The RNA evidence for the magnitude is M2h's (`ac5580b`) and M2i's (`f6e71c6`) and is not re-read here

sources.accession: the committed .bio programmes of this checkout
genomeos.bio's own `# test:` checks, run in process

inputs.path: the contact tables the C. elegans programmes read as they parse

parameters.method: sha256 per programme and over the group; counts from bio.main(['test', ...])

exclusions: no model request, no key, no network, no money; nothing is fitted and no RNA is read

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

partitions.none: one population, the committed programmes; no partition is taken and none is implied

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 0f068e2

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
